title: Real-Time Structural Health Monitoring of the Bolueta Railway Bridge During Track Renewal Works: A Case Study
content: This paper presents a real-time, data-driven Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) system deployed on the Bolueta railway bridge (Bilbao, Spain), a singular bridge with a continuous configuration comprising a multi-span double-box-girder deck, V-shaped piers, and a twin-rib arch. The bridge was monitored during an approximately one-year track renewal campaign involving concrete chipping works on the ballastless track, requiring monitoring during both nighttime rehabilitation activities and uninterrupted normal railway operation. The implemented monitoring system is based on a modular architecture using MQTT over a 4G network for continuous data transmission, storage, visualization, and processing. The recorded data comprise acceleration, strain, relative displacement, and inclination measurements. Global finite element models were complementarily used for offline baseline verification by comparing their predictions with the measurements ob-tained from the monitoring system. To support operational decision-making, a real-time monitoring platform incorporating threshold-based alerts, machine-learning-based anomaly detection using identified natural frequencies (centered on a dense neural network classifier) and acceleration time histories (convolutional autoencoder), and a data contextualization tool was deployed. The results showed good agreement between measurements and numerical predictions, while no persistent deviation from the monitored reference condition was identified during the monitoring period. This case study demonstrates the applicability of modular, online, data-based SHM systems for supporting the assessment and management of railway bridges during complex maintenance operations.
